reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that no redline or comment was proposed — the rendered text is identical to the original paragraphs, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to assess.

The cited clauses support the compliance call for our party (Sanofi): 10.1(a) directs Third Party invention assignments to the engaging Party (so work generated for Sanofi vests in Sanofi), 6.2 assigns all Regulatory Approvals/INDs/NDAs to Sanofi, 10.5(a) gives Sanofi sole ownership of Product Marks, 3.2 is only a narrow performance-limited sublicence back to RevMed, and 3.6 negates implied licences — no assignment of our IP or data to the counterparty.

Joint Program Technology is correctly analysed: joint ownership paired with a right to exploit and license without accounting or consent, plus a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable cross-licence, meets the fallback (unrestricted right to exploit) rather than walk-away territory, and the rationale expressly flags this as sitting at the fallback rather than treating it as a deviation — the correct playbook classification.
The deterministic check ('no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains') passes, corroborating the direction of the ownership provisions.

The rationale appropriately discloses the residual uncertainty from the redacted [***] allocation in 10.1(a) and the Article XII reversion as bargained-for, so the compliant conclusion is transparently qualified rather than overstated; retained as internal evidence, not raised as a negotiation issue.
